newsitem.title: USA: Clinton concerned at lack of fast-track authority.
newsitem.headline: Clinton concerned at lack of fast-track authority.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton urged Congress on Tuesday to give him fast-track authority to negotiate an expansion of the NAFTA trade pact to include Chile.
"I am very concerned that we have not passed fast-track authority in this country," Clinton said at a joint news conference with Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien.
Chretien said he hoped Clinton would be able to convince Congress to proceed on the authority for Chile. "It's urgent that we move becasue some are getting impatient in South America," he said.

Fast-track authority will allow U.S. trade officials to negotiate trade deals without fear Congress will change them. Lawmakers would be able to vote for an agreement or against it, but would not be allowed to amend it.
Clinton had the authority to negotiate the North American Free Trade Agreement between the United States, Canada and Mexico, and wants it again to negotiate a deal with Chile.
"I think we have to do it. It's clear that expanding trade will strengthen democracy in Latin America and will strengthen our hand in the second-fastest growing area in the world," Clinton said.

Republican congressional leaders, generally supportive of free-trade agreements, have told the White House that some Democrats in Congress need to support fast track in order to muster the votes needed to pass the legislation.
